title: Fixed-window rate limiter
description: Requests arrive at the given times (whole seconds, never negative, in non-decreasing order). Time is cut into fixed windows of window seconds: window 0 covers times 0 to window - 1, window 1 covers times window to 2 * window - 1, and so on. Each window allows at most limit requests; the count starts again from zero in every new window. For each request, in order: if its window still has room, print `t=T allowed (K/LIMIT)`, where K is how many requests of that window have been allowed so far, this one included; otherwise print `t=T blocked`. After the last request print `blocked: B` with the number of blocked requests and return B as a success value. Blocked requests do not use up room. If window is less than 1, return the error `window must be positive` and print nothing; otherwise, if limit is negative, return the error `limit must not be negative` and print nothing (the window is checked first). A limit of 0 blocks every request. An empty list prints only `blocked: 0`.

visible_examples.stdout:
t=0 allowed (1/2)
t=1 allowed (2/2)
t=2 blocked
blocked: 1

notes: Level 3. Window number is floor division of non-negative times by a positive window (no negative operands anywhere); the counter resets on a window change, also when the previous window had blocked requests; the first request always starts a fresh window (time 0 included); two settings errors, window checked first, both print nothing; summary line printed on success only. Largest time and window 9e15; naive Math.floor(t / window) is exact on every test input.
